fact: La Poste Tunisienne provides students with e-Dinar wallets and electronic payment cards for university financial operations including the payment of university scholarships and loans.

The World Bank says 44.4% of the cash transfers under Tunisia's AMEN Program have been digitalized, and a convention between the Ministry of Social Affairs and the Tunisian Post continues digital payment cards tied to an e-wallet for AMEN beneficiaries.

Tunisia Post manages about 970,000 accounts for disadvantaged families, low-income households and retirees, about 65% of pensions are withdrawn through ATMs and 400,000 e-wallets are active, per African Manager.
